LoloBuy restricted items guide: check before you buy

A product can be legal to sell yet unsuitable for one carrier, export channel or destination. Check the exact item before payment so the warehouse is not the first place you discover a restriction.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s current public mail-restriction, export, inspection, delivery and route materials, checked on 22 October 2026. Restrictions can change by product, packaging, carrier, route and destination. Use the live order and parcel screens, and obtain a case-specific answer when eligibility is unclear.

“Restricted” is not one decision

Before buying through an agent, separate four questions. Can LoloBuy purchase the item? Can it enter and remain in the warehouse? Does an international shipping line accept the finished parcel? Can the recipient lawfully import and receive it? A “yes” at one stage does not answer the others.

LoloBuy’s mail-restriction material says the warehouse marks items with a prohibited icon when they fall into a mail-restricted category. Its export list also says the platform may add, remove or change listed categories and does not guarantee that its list is complete, current or accurate. That is an important limitation: a static help article is an early warning tool, not a permanent clearance certificate.

The strongest time to investigate is before the shopping agent buys. If you wait until stock-in, money may already have been spent on the product and Chinese domestic delivery. A seller may not accept a return, and a different route may cost more or still be unavailable.

Start with the physical product, not its marketing title

Restrictions attach to what the item is made of, contains and does. The seller title may omit the feature that matters to a carrier. “Portable light” could contain a removable battery, an installed battery or no battery. “Beauty set” may include liquid, powder, gel, aerosol, alcohol or a pressurised container. “Accessory” might contain a magnet, blade or radio transmitter.

Open the full listing and record the exact model, materials, ingredients or contents, quantity, unit size, battery chemistry and capacity where stated, and whether any cell can be removed. Note liquids, gels, powders, pastes, food, medicine, supplements, tobacco, alcohol, e-cigarette components, magnets, compressed containers, sharp parts, plants, seeds or animal-derived materials. This is a screening list, not a claim that every item in those categories is always banned.

For electronics, identify whether the seller ships the device with a battery and whether spare batteries are included. For cosmetics, distinguish a solid product from a liquid or aerosol. For sets, inspect every component rather than classifying the bundle from its main item. One small component can determine the parcel’s route options.

Distinguish prohibited goods from route-sensitive goods

LoloBuy’s published export material includes broad prohibited or controlled categories such as weapons and imitation weapons, explosives, narcotics, potent poisons, certain dangerous chemicals, currency, protected cultural property, endangered animals or plants and some medical or communications equipment. It also refers to counterfeit and pirated goods and warns that the list is not exhaustive.

Do not use that summary to decide that an unmentioned product is automatically permitted. Legal definitions can be more specific than a seller’s wording, and destination rules can add restrictions that do not appear in an origin-country list. When a product touches a controlled category, obtain current professional or official guidance before purchase.

Other products may be carrier-sensitive rather than universally prohibited. Batteries, liquids, powders, gels, food and magnetic items can face different conditions by line. The product may need particular documentation, packaging or a specialised route, or it may have no available route for the selected destination. Eligibility must therefore be checked against the exact product and the live route terms.

Ask a question the agent can verify

A useful pre-purchase enquiry contains facts, not a generic “Can this ship?” Send the direct seller link, exact option and model, destination country, quantity and the feature that may trigger a restriction. If the item includes a battery, provide the seller’s stated battery type and capacity. If it is a liquid or powder, provide the product type, unit amount and total quantity without guessing.

Ask two separate questions: “Can the shopping agent purchase and warehouse this exact item?” and “Which currently displayed lines accept it for my destination?” A reply about purchasing does not guarantee an international line. A reply that a carrier may review the item is also not a promise of acceptance or customs clearance.

Save the dated answer with the listing details. If the seller changes the option, quantity, formula or included accessories, ask again. The answer belongs to the item described at that time; it should not be copied to a similar-looking listing.

Read the warehouse flag correctly

The prohibited icon described in LoloBuy’s FAQ is a warning that the warehouse item involves a mail restriction. It does not necessarily explain whether the issue comes from law, platform policy, aviation safety, a carrier rule or missing information. Open the item details and ask what product characteristic created the flag.

The same FAQ says users who understand the category can ask customer service to check with a logistics provider. Treat that as a request for review, not a method for bypassing a rule. Do not ask support to rename, conceal or misclassify the product. If a provider cannot accept it, choose a lawful alternative, pursue any currently available seller return, or leave it out of the international parcel.

LoloBuy’s inspection scope says all goods undergo a prohibited-item check. Standard visual inspection, however, does not prove chemical composition, hidden battery specifications, authenticity or professional product function. If eligibility depends on information the warehouse cannot observe, obtain documentation from the seller before purchase.

One restricted item can affect a combined parcel

LoloBuy’s mail-restriction FAQ says that when part of a warehouse order involves restrictions, other items submitted in the same delivery order may also become restricted. This is why a single sensitive product should not be treated as an afterthought in a large haul.

Build two parcel scenarios before paying international shipping. Scenario A combines only clearly compatible goods. Scenario B isolates the flagged item and checks whether a lawful route appears for it. Compare eligible routes, chargeable weight, packaging and risk for both. Splitting can preserve route choices for ordinary goods, but it is not automatically cheaper and does not make the isolated item eligible.

Do not mix sensitive goods with clothing or ordinary products in an attempt to hide them. Some older LoloBuy help text contains quantity and mixing suggestions that may not reflect current carrier or destination rules. The live line restrictions and lawful declaration are the relevant controls.

Check destination rules independently

A route appearing in the parcel screen does not guarantee that US or European authorities will admit the contents. Food, medicine, supplements, cosmetics, plant material, animal products, radio equipment and intellectual-property-sensitive goods can be regulated differently by destination. The recipient may need permits, identity information, product documents or payment of duties and taxes.

LoloBuy’s delivery agreement says parcel processing can involve product information and recipient identity details for import and export declarations. It also identifies customs action and government safety rules as risks outside ordinary platform control. Before dispatch, confirm current destination requirements with the appropriate authority or a qualified professional when the product is regulated.

Do not rely on a customer anecdote that a similar parcel passed once. Customs inspection is not a certification process for future shipments. A previous delivery can show only what happened to that parcel under those facts and at that time.

Declaration cannot repair ineligibility

The product name, quantity and value on the customs declaration should match the order and the physical item. Calling a battery “parts,” a liquid “accessories” or a branded product “gift” does not change its transport or import category. It creates conflicting records and can increase the risk of delay, return, seizure or loss.

Use a specific plain-language description and a supportable value. The customs declaration guide explains how to make those records consistent. It does not provide a workaround for prohibited goods.

Pre-order restricted-item checklist

Identity: Exact seller link, model, option and every component in the set.
Contents: Materials, ingredients, liquid or powder form, magnets, blades and pressurised parts.
Battery: Installed, removable or spare; chemistry and capacity when the seller states them.
Quantity: Unit amount and total amount, without relying on a generic listing photo.
Purchase stage: Written confirmation that the agent can buy and warehouse the exact option.
Route stage: Current lines that accept the item and finished packaging for the destination.
Destination: Import restrictions, documents and recipient obligations checked separately.
Parcel plan: Effect on ordinary items and a split-parcel comparison if necessary.
Declaration: Accurate product description, quantity and value that match the evidence.
Fallback: A lawful decision if no route accepts the item; never conceal or rename it.

Conclusion: verify the item before it becomes warehouse stock

A reliable LoloBuy restricted items check follows the physical product through four gates: purchase, warehouse, carrier and destination. Identify the risk-triggering feature, ask a precise pre-purchase question, keep the answer with the listing, and re-check live route terms after the item is packed.

No static list can guarantee eligibility. When the product details or rules are unclear, pause instead of assuming that a seller title, warehouse icon or available route proves compliance. To research ordinary products before applying this check, open FindSpreadsheet →
